newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-TURNER EQUALS COURSE RECORD TO SNARE LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TURNER EQUALS COURSE RECORD TO SNARE LEAD.

text.p: New Zealander Greg Turner equalled the course record with a seven under par 65 to take a one shot lead after the first round of the A$1.2 million ($925,000) Heineken Classic on Thursday.
Turner picked up six strokes on the back nine of the tight Vines resort course with an eagle and four birdies to be one shot clear of compatriot Frank Nobilo.
South African Ernie Els, winner of the Johnnie Walker Classic in Queensland on Sunday, struggled to a 73 and will almost certainly need to improve on that score to avoid missing the cut.
Australian Wayne Grady and England's Miles Tunnicliff share third place on 67.
American Fred Couples led a group of four players one shot further back on 68 in a tournament jointly sanctioned by the European and Australasian tours.
"I finished second here in 1991 and shot 66 in the first round last year. I like Thursdays at The Vines," said Turner, who raced up the leaderboard after arriving on the ninth tee on level par.
"I missed only one fairway, and that was only by a yard, and two greens. But even then I was on the fringe," added Turner, who said he had been troubled by a wrist tendon injury since 1992.
After sharing the lead in the first round last year, Turner faded to finish in joint 17th behind eventual winner Ian Woosnam.
The Welshman, one of five players who now share the course record with Turner, began his defence of the title with a level par 72.
Scotland's Colin Montgomerie, who is seeking to become Europe's top golfer for a fifth year in succession, opened with a two-under par 70, a score matched by American John Daly.
